note: Deep-dive #17. Two resource groups plus anything Site Recovery adds: all must be gone at the end. Initial replication can take a long time: record replication and failover only afterwards. If the gate says NOT READY, show it and say why.
prepare: python -m pip install -q -r requirements.txt; python -m pytest -q
# owner signs in (device code), not recorded
az vm list-skus -l westeurope --size Standard_D2s_v5 -o table

Push-Location src; python -m migplan check ../build/all.json --landing-zone 10.60.0.0/16; python -m migplan plan ../build/all.json; python -m migplan csv ../build/all.json --out ../build/import.csv; Pop-Location
az deployment sub create -l westeurope -n mglab17 -f infra/main.bicep -p infra/main.bicepparam --query properties.outputs -o json

# manual (portal): Azure Migrate > Create project in rg-mglab-deep-dive-17, geography Europe; Discover > Import using CSV > upload build/import.csv; wait for Completed (download the warning CSV if there are warnings)
# manual (portal): Assess > Azure VM > Imported servers, target West Europe; create one as-is and one performance-based assessment, note the comfort factor
# manual (portal): VM con-app01 > Disaster recovery > North Europe, vault rsv-mglab-dr, target network vnet-target; wait for initial replication to finish and note the time
# manual (portal): run a test failover (latest recovery point, vnet-target) before recording the failover screen, or record the NOT READY gate first

screens.name: import
steps: Azure Migrate > the project in rg-mglab-deep-dive-17 > Servers, databases and web apps
Azure Migrate: Discovery and assessment > Discovered servers > Import based tab
Show the import status Completed and the imported servers: the real lab VMs from the collector plus the fictional Contoso rows

screens.name: assessment
steps: Open the Azure VM assessment created for the imported group (West Europe)
Summary: Azure VM readiness counts and the estimated monthly cost
Azure VM readiness tab: the recommended size per server
If time allows show both the performance-based and the as-is assessment and say which settings each used

screens.name: replication
steps: Recovery Services vault rsv-mglab-dr (North Europe) > Replicated items > con-app01
Overview: replication health, status Protected, the RPO and the time it was last computed, Failover readiness
Record only after initial replication has finished
mask: resource ids and storage account names

screens.name: failover
also: Left half of the split (browser, labadmin): portal > Replicated items > con-app01 > Test failover (latest recovery point, non-production target network), the job succeeding, the test VM in the North Europe group, then Cleanup test failover. The terminal shows PASS lines and READY, or the real FAIL lines (say why in the narration).

teardown: # manual (portal): VM con-app01 > Disaster recovery > Disable replication (stops Site Recovery billing); remove the Site Recovery extension if the VM is reused
az group delete -n rg-mglab-deep-dive-17-dr --yes   # if the vault refuses, remove replicated items and the Site Recovery configuration first, then retry
Remove-Item build -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item src/items.json -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
# manual: list the resource groups again and delete any group Site Recovery created for replica disks (check each group's resources first); confirm the Azure Migrate project is gone
needs: paid:VM con-app01, Site Recovery protected instance, replica disks, test failover VM, cache storage (delete same day)
